data.description: The C11-192 classifier gives 'runloop-idle' its own bucket: main parked at the top of the run loop in mach_msg2_trap/CFRunLoopServiceMachPort while the watchdog heartbeat went unserviced (10 of 875 captures, pre-#401 counts). If main is genuinely idle, the heartbeat should have been serviced, so these are either a watchdog false positive (e.g. clock jump, App Nap, machine sleep race) or a real scheduling starvation worth knowing about. Deliverable: a decision, recorded on this ticket, of whether runloop-idle events keep reporting to Sentry, report with a distinguishing tag, or are suppressed as known-benign, plus the one-line code change if suppression/tagging is chosen.
data.title: Decide whether runloop-idle hang captures should report at all

data.body:
DECISION: suppress runloop-idle from Sentry unconditionally, and stop letting the bucket swallow nested run loops. PR #413 (branch fix/C11-198-runloop-idle).

METHOD. Classified all 21,253 captures / 5,360 episodes in ~/Library/Logs/c11/hang.log (Jun 15 - Aug 9, 55 pids) with the rules as shipped on main (b2fb5caa5). The port reproduces #402/#411's published distribution (lock-wait 44.8% vs their 45.8%, runloop-idle 37.3% vs 37.4%), so it measures the same thing. runloop-idle is 2,491 of 5,360 episodes (46.6%), matching #411's 46.5%.

FINDING: the bucket is TWO populations, and the ticket's framing (false positive vs starvation) is a false dichotomy.

(1) 2,414 episodes, 96.9%, 54 pids: main parked in -[NSApplication run] -> _DPSNextEvent -> ReceiveNextEventCommon, blocked on the event port. That is an app READY TO DEQUEUE THE NEXT USER EVENT. Not starvation, not a wedge, and not visible to anyone. All three runloop-idle events Sentry has ever received (C11-3C) are exactly that stack: byte-identical, 21 frames, nothing of ours below main. Unactionable by construction (no phase, no culprit, no c11 frame at any depth), and under the global SentryEventBudgetGate ceiling it spends budget a real wedge needed. Supporting: against a 2000ms threshold with a 250ms tick, only 12.3% of these episodes are first detected at the 2000-2250ms floor; p50 first detection is 4,110ms and p90 is 35,813ms, so the watchdog itself routinely missed 8 to 130+ consecutive ticks before noticing. A watchdog that late is not in a position to certify another thread stalled.

(2) 77 episodes, 3.1%: NESTED run loops the app enters on purpose, where main is genuinely blocked and our own frames are on the stack. BrowserPanel.presentInsecureHTTPAlert (6 episodes, 1 pid, median 8.5 min, max 6.8 HOURS) and TerminalController.v2AwaitCallback spinning CFRunLoopRun on main for a WKWebView callback (70 episodes, 12 pids). These are real and actionable, and the shipped policy DROPS them whenever the window is unwatched, which for socket-driven browser automation is most of the time.

VERDICT ON THE PRIOR POLICY. C11-191 / PR #411 was right in direction (own fingerprint bucket + conditional suppression) but its watched exception rests on a premise the stack refutes: 'the UI went dead while they watched' is not what -[NSApplication run] -> _DPSNextEvent means. Watchedness does not change what the stack says. So #411 did NOT already close this ticket; it left both a false-positive residue that still reports and an actionable class that gets suppressed.

CODE CHANGE (PR #413, two edits):
  - MainThreadHangSignature.cause: require '-[NSApplication run]' in the 16-frame cause window for runLoopIdleCause. On the corpus this separates the two populations EXACTLY: present on all 2,895 outermost-idle captures, absent from all 5,031 nested ones, zero misclassifications either way. Nested captures fall through to the existing module rules (appkit / other) and report with hang.culprit naming the frame that entered the loop.
  - MainThreadHangMonitor.isWorthReporting: drops the visibility argument; runloop-idle never reports. AppVisibility.isWatched removed with the gate it existed for; appIsActive / hasVisibleWindow still ride along as hang.app_active / hang.window_visible tags and in the log header.
Simulated over the corpus: runloop-idle 2,492 -> 2,415 episodes (all now silent), appkit / other gain the 77 real ones. Nothing is lost: every capture still lands in the local hang log and PostHog.

RELEASE-STATE CAVEAT. 0.63.0+124 (the build behind the three C11-3C events) predates #411, so those events carry no hang.app_active tag. No post-#411 build has produced a runloop-idle Sentry event yet, i.e. #411's suppression has never been exercised in the field. The public line is still on the pre-#402 fingerprint (C11-30 3,982ev/20u, C11-31 2,799ev/17u, both still arriving as of Aug 10). Do not read C11-3C's volume as a signal.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH A TICKET (not in scope here): BrowserPanel.presentInsecureHTTPAlert blocked one pid for 6.8 hours. A modal alert that can wedge c11 for hours with no timeout is a real bug; #413 only makes it visible in Sentry instead of filed as benign idle.

Ticket can close once #413 merges.

data.body:
CI GREEN on PR #413. All required checks pass: build (5m35s, '** TEST SUCCEEDED **' on the c11LogicTests gate), compat-tests, build-ghosttykit, web-typecheck, workflow-guard-tests, remote-daemon-tests, and all four drawbridge jobs.

New tests confirmed executing in the gate:
  MainThreadHangReportingRuleTests.testAnIdleRunLoopIsNeverWorthReporting  passed
  MainThreadHangReportingRuleTests.testEveryOtherCauseReports              passed
  MainThreadHangSignatureTests.testANestedRunLoopIsNotClassifiedAsIdle     passed
  MainThreadHangSignatureTests.testIdleRunLoopIsSeparatedFromAWedgeInCompute passed

The 'Host-bound unit tests (advisory)' step is red, but it is advisory/non-blocking and every failure is pre-existing and unrelated (BrowserPanelRemoteStoreTests, BrowserThemeSettingsTests, BrowserWindowPortalLifecycleTests, CommandPalette*, ConversationScraperTests). No MainThreadHang test fails there.

Follow-up filed: C11-204, the app-modal runModal wedge in BrowserPanel.presentInsecureHTTPAlert (linked related_to this ticket).

C11-198 is ready to close on merge of #413.

PR #413 merged to main 2026-08-12 (squash) with all eleven CI checks green, including the 'build' job which is the compile plus c11LogicTests gate. The four hang tests covering the new -[NSApplication run] discriminator and the unconditional runloop-idle suppression passed there.

Operator reviewed and approved the reversal of #411's visibility gate on the merits: if main is sitting in -[NSApplication run] -> _DPSNextEvent it is available to dequeue events, so an unserviced heartbeat means the background-QoS watchdog thread lost the CPU, not that the app froze. Who was watching cannot change that, which was the premise #411's gate rested on. The population is retained in the local hang log and PostHog under the same cause label, so nothing is lost, and a revert is available if the post-0.63.0 field data contradicts the local-log inference.

Decision recorded, code shipped, ticket satisfied.

Reviewed the diff and the reasoning before merge.

The classification narrowing is the strongest part and I checked it independently: requiring -[NSApplication run] in the cause window is validated as present on all 2,895 outermost-idle captures and absent from all 5,031 nested ones, zero misclassification across 7,926 real captures. That is not a heuristic, it is a clean separator, and it is what unblocked the nested-runloop cases that #411 was wrongly suppressing. C11-204 (app-modal alert wedging c11 for up to 6.8 hours) was invisible precisely because of that suppression, which is the concrete proof the narrowing was needed.

The reporting change is the contested half and it holds up. _DPSNextEvent means main is blocked on the event port and ready to dequeue, so the app was not unavailable to anyone; the delayed heartbeat is a watchdog-thread scheduling fact, not an app-freeze fact, and window visibility is orthogonal to it. Also material: the three runloop-idle events Sentry ever received came from 0.63.0+124, which predates #411, so its visibility gate has never actually run in the field and was never validated by anything but reasoning.

Cost of being wrong is bounded: the population still lands in the local hang log and PostHog under the same cause label, so the data is retained and a revert restores reporting. Approved and merged.
